extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and parties in inter partes review (IPR) proceedings (petitioners, patent owners, counsel, and expert witnesses)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and evidentiary criteria the PTAB applies when evaluating obviousness challenges in an IPR, including what a petitioner must show to combine prior-art references, proof burdens, and when testimony or evidence is credited or excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Particularity requirement for petitions (35 U.S.C. §312(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: "the petition identifies, in writing and with particularity, each claim challenged, the grounds on which the challenge to each claim is based, and the evidence that supports the grounds for the challenge to each claim."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petitioner must explain specifically how the references would be combined to produce the claimed invention; merely reciting individual teachings without tying them to particular limitations is insufficient. (Text cites §312(a)(3) and Lowe’s v. Epistar.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Motivation to combine prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner must identify a motivation to combine the teachings of the asserted references such that a person of ordinary skill in the art (POSITA) would be prompted to make the combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motivation can be shown by explicit statements in the petition (e.g., pages 66–70 here) explaining benefits of combining (e.g., adding richer metadata for better organization). General or conclusory statements are insufficient; the Board found the Petition's stated motivations here persuasive because they provided a roadmap and cited evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear, evidence-supported account of the contemplated workings of the combination
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'clear, evidence-supported account of the contemplated workings of the combination is a prerequisite' to adequately explain and support a conclusion that a skilled artisan would be motivated to combine and reasonably expect success (Personal Web Techs.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners should explain which portions of each reference correspond to which claim limitations and how the combined system would operate. Anti-pattern: describing references individually without showing how their teachings interact to meet claim limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: No pick-and-choose / mix-and-match approach
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner cannot merely show that elements of a claim were independently known in the prior art; the Board disfavors an approach that asks the factfinder to interpret which parts of multiple references would be combined without a clear roadmap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite specific passages showing which reference supplies each limitation. Avoid broad citations spanning many columns/pages and then asking the Board to infer the combination. Case cites: KSR, Personal Web, Trend Micro, Lyft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable expectation of success
rubrics_metrics.description: Obviousness requires that a POSITA would have had a reasonable expectation of success in making the proposed modification or combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The expectation need not include literal code or physical lines when the modification is within ordinary skill; bodily incorporation is not required. But if a petitioner relies on nontrivial integration, some showing that implementation would be within ordinary skill or routine is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bodily incorporation not required
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioners need not show literal transplantation of specific code or structure from a secondary reference into the primary reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It's sufficient to rely on a reference's general teaching (e.g., 'using thumbnails to represent albums/folders') rather than proposing to copy specific lines of OS code. But petitioners still must show why a POSITA would make the modification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching away
rubrics_metrics.description: If a primary reference teaches away from the proposed modification because it would undermine the reference’s core functionality, that weighs against obviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent Owner argued Horn taught away by prioritizing space efficiency; the Board rejected the teaching-away argument where Horn already used thumbnails for individual objects and the modification did not conflict with core functionality. To show teaching away, a party must explain why the modification would conflict with intended function with reasoned evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credibility and sufficiency of expert testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: Expert testimony that is conclusory or not adequately explained may be given little or no weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board will discount testimony that fails to identify specific facts or reasoning (e.g., Dr. Balakrishnan's conclusory assertion about processing overhead without explanation). Experts should identify concrete technical obstacles or integration challenges if relying on them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printed publication and date requirement for prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: To use a reference as prior art, a petitioner must establish that it is a printed publication with a publication date prior to the patent's effective filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to prove a reference (e.g., WinTV) is a printed publication with an appropriate date defeats reliance on that reference. Evidence and foundation showing publication and date are necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preponderance of the evidence burden
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner must prove unpatentability (e.g., obviousness) by a preponderance of the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institution and final decisions are based on whether the petitioner has met that evidentiary burden for the challenged claims. The Board explicitly states petitioner proved claims 1–6 and 9–13 unpatentable by a preponderance here, but not claims 7,8,14,15 due to WinTV issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing implementation feasibility / compatibility issues
rubrics_metrics.description: When an argument to combine references would require significant hardware or software integration, the petitioner should address compatibility and implementation feasibility or explain why such integration is routine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent Owner argued Horn’s OS architecture was incompatible with Chao’s thumbnails; the Board found the argument misplaced where petitioner did not propose bodily incorporation and where the primary reference already used similar features. If relying on incompatibility, the patent owner must identify specific challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design-choice obviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a claimed feature is a design choice among known alternatives, it may be deemed an obvious design choice to a POSITA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: choosing a thumbnail instead of a generic folder icon was considered a design choice and obvious in light of the prior art's disclosures; petitioners can argue such choices would have been within routine design decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity for showing discrete claim limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: For each limitation, the petitioner must tie claimed language to specific disclosure in the prior art or show obviousness of the limitation with reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent Owner criticized petitions that assert Kaplan-Bryant combinations but fail to state which reference supports which limitation (illustrated by the PO's table mapping limitations to petition discussion). The Board looks to the petition plus any roadmap pages to determine sufficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of pointers/indexed databases supports certain functional claim effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosures showing an indexed database with pointers to a single physical file support claim limitations concerning representation of the same object in multiple collections and deletion semantics (i.e., deleting a pointer vs physical file).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kaplan's ¶44 (indexed file stores a pointer) was persuasive to the Board to show limitation 1[l]/9[j] where a single physical file can be represented in multiple collections such that deleting from one collection need not delete the file from another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition roadmap can cure apparent pick-and-choose gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition's general roadmap pages that explain the proposed combination can supply the detail missing from per-claim explanations, and the Board will read specific claim analyses in light of that roadmap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent Owner argued the petition inconsistently relied on Kaplan or Bryant for various limitations; the Board found the petition's pages 66–70 provided a sufficient roadmap tying references together for the per-claim analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural sufficiency for motions to exclude
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion to exclude must state reasons for exclusion; if the underlying evidentiary issue becomes moot, the motion may be dismissed as moot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board dismissed Patent Owner's Motion to Exclude as moot where it had already concluded WinTV was not proven to be a prior printed publication and where some exhibits were not before the Board due to denial of supplemental submission.
